key_insight: Deposition-defined tiers at ~6 nm pitch would put many bits in one etchable stack height. Wafer-scale low-temperature TMD growth makes sequential 2D tiers thinkable.
killer_doubt: At 99.9% per-tier yield, 1000 sequential growths leave 37% of stacks intact. A vertical gate sees a ~1 nm sheet edge. MoS2 (1.8 eV) leaks more than IGZO (3.2 eV).
decisive_experiment: MOCVD a 10-tier MoS2/hBN superlattice at <=450 C on 200 mm. Build edge-gated FETs through one etched hole. Measure per-tier Ion/Ioff, the spread and tier-to-tier coupling (~$300k). Stop if Ion is under 1 uA.
prior_art: MIT (J. Kim) growth-based monolithic 3D TMD stacks (Nature 2024); Penn State and Fudan 2D integration; Samsung SAIT 2D channels (training knowledge).

key_insight: A transistor-less, capacitor-less vertical charge-shift string has one sense node per string. Its writes stay in a semiconductor channel, so it avoids the write-endurance wall.
killer_doubt: 128 tiers in 3 phases hold ~42 packets. At imec's >98% CTE, 0.98^128 leaves 7%. 60-130 ns access needs ~1 GHz clocks against the 4-6 MHz demonstrated.
decisive_experiment: Build a 16-gate vertical IGZO CCD string in a university fab. Measure per-transfer CTE against clock rate from 1 to 500 MHz at 85 C (~$250k). Stop if CTE is below 0.9995 above 100 MHz.
prior_art: imec IGZO CCD buffer memory: planar 142-bit (IEDM 2024), vertical (IMW 2026), per earlier stage-2 search logs. Phase B N-08; 1970s CCD memories.

key_insight: Closed-flux circumferential rings have no stray field and read non-destructively. A magnetic write sidesteps the charge-fluence endurance wall, one of triage's four safe write routes.
killer_doubt: A 2% MR segment on a ~1.5 kohm pillar gives ~24 uV at 50 uA, below ~50 uV Johnson noise at 100 MHz. Oersted writes need ~5-10 mA.
decisive_experiment: ALD a NiFe/Cu/CoFe shell into 40 nm holes through a 4-strap stack. Measure per-segment delta-R and the half-select write margin (~$200k). Stop if delta-R is under 1 ohm per segment.
prior_art: UNIVAC/Bell plated-wire memory (1960s); IBM racetrack (Parkin); Phase B N-82 racetrack-in-hole; I-08865 (another batch) dropped an inductive variant (training knowledge).

key_insight: Inference weights are written rarely. A field-programmable OTP tier in the accelerator BEOL streams them at sub-pJ/bit with no refresh, freeing HBM for KV cache. One SKU serves any model.
killer_doubt: Rewritable High Bandwidth Flash (SanDisk/SK hynix) targets 8-16x HBM capacity for weights. An 8-deck crosspoint gives ~2.4 Gb/mm2. Models churn every ~3-6 months and strand burned dies.
decisive_experiment: Build a 2-deck OTS-selector oxide-antifuse crosspoint at <=400 C on a foundry BEOL coupon. Measure program yield, read margin and disturb over 1e12 reads, and model decode tokens/s per dollar against HBF (~$400k).
prior_art: Matrix Semiconductor/SanDisk 3D OTP (2001-05); Taalas hard-wired-model silicon; SanDisk + SK hynix High Bandwidth Flash for inference weights (training knowledge).

key_insight: Gain before the latch could, in principle, read a few-hundred-electron node. Triage already solves the read side without gain: charge transfer (N-04) cuts Cs 10x.
killer_doubt: SPAD breakdown is ~10-25 V against a 3 V wordline floor. Guard rings need um pitch at 30-40 nm. A 0.1 fF node needs <0.5 fA, 26x below the tail.
decisive_experiment: No new experiment is justified. To revive it, run TCAD (~$30k) on a sub-100 nm pitch junction and show breakdown under 5 V, gain of at least 30 and no edge breakdown.
prior_art: Z-RAM impact-ionisation floating body; EMCCD gain registers; Fossum QIS jots. The same verdict was given on I-02889 and I-05065 in other batches (training knowledge).

key_insight: Panel lines already run IGZO TFTs on ~5.5 m2 substrates with no EUV. A 2T0C gain cell needs no HAR capacitor, so the cell process matches their toolset.
killer_doubt: FPD steppers resolve ~1.2-1.5 um, not 0.5 um, and Gen-8.5 has no ArF tool. At F=1.5 um, 8F2 is 18 um2: ~7 GB/m2 per tier, 9x below claim.
decisive_experiment: Merge into I-00145's partner run. First, a free check: get actual Gen-8.5 stepper resolution and overlay specs from Canon/Nikon. Stop if F is above 0.8 um.
prior_art: Near-duplicate of I-00145. SEL CAAC-IGZO DOSRAM/NOSRAM; Sharp/JDI memory-in-pixel; Phase B N-36/N-38 glass and panel oxide memory (training knowledge).

key_insight: Accept ~1% defective cells across a panel and cover them with block codes, so panel yield is not the gate. That twist should be folded into I-00145.
killer_doubt: At 1-1.5 um rules, 4 tiers give ~7-16 GB/m2 per tier, about $10-22/GB. That is 7-15x DDR5's $1.48/GB cost and viable only while contract prices stay near $20/GB.
decisive_experiment: Merge into I-00145. Add a defect-map study: on one partner panel run, measure the cell-fail clustering and size the block-code overhead needed for 1e-15 UBER (~$50k analysis on top).
prior_art: Near-duplicate of I-00145. RCA Weimer TFT (1962); SEL CAAC-IGZO memory; memory-in-pixel LCDs; Phase B N-38 (training knowledge).

key_insight: Depreciated Gen-8.5 oxide-TFT lines are EUV-free, helium-light capacity outside DRAM fabs. Transistor-written gain cells need no HAR capacitor, so a slow CXL tier fits their tools.
killer_doubt: At ~1.5 um (the FPD stepper limit), ~7-10 GB/m2 per tier costs ~$15-25/GB. That matches only today's ~$20/GB contract price; if prices normalize to ~$5/GB, the idea dies.
decisive_experiment: Do one Gen-6/8.5 partner run at minimum rules: 2T0C test arrays plus n-only IGZO sense amps. Measure cell area, retention at 85 C and Vt sigma, then feed a mask-count cost model (~$300k).
prior_art: No DRAM-on-display-line product found (R17 search). SEL DOSRAM/NOSRAM on Si; Phase B N-36/N-38; I-10785 ADVANCE and I-03879 DROP in other batches.

key_insight: Self-organized eutectic conductors could replace a high-aspect-ratio etch-and-fill with crystal growth. It is a genuinely unseen use of in-situ composites.
killer_doubt: Si-TaSi2 rods are ~1 um wide at ~1e6-1e7 per cm2. Spacing scales as V^-1/2, so 100 nm pitch needs ~900x faster solidification. Random rod positions cannot align with periodic wordlines.
decisive_experiment: First, a free paper check: compile published Si-TaSi2 lambda-squared-times-V data and stop if 200 nm pitch needs over 10 cm/min. Only then, one float-zone run at maximum rate with SEM pitch mapping (~$100k).
prior_art: Directionally solidified Si-TaSi2 in-situ composites (Ditchek, GTE Labs, 1980s) used for field-emitter and Schottky arrays (training knowledge).

key_insight: Doping-selective porosification turns a low-strain Si/Si:B epi stack into many single-crystal tiers. Boron at 1e19 strains ~150x less than Si0.8Ge0.2, so tier count escapes the SiGe relaxation limit.
killer_doubt: Holes injected from deeper p+ layers destroy selectivity (a 1990s patent anodizes top-first), and n- tiers block current at reverse junctions. No data beyond a few levels; 50-100 needed.
decisive_experiment: Buy a 20-period p+ (1e19) / lightly doped RPCVD epi stack (~$30k). Etch slits and anodize laterally at several current densities. Use TEM/EBSD on every tier for selectivity, pore-front uniformity and crystal survival (~$150k).
prior_art: US5023200 multi-level porous-Si buried insulators; NTT FIPOS (1980s); Canon ELTRAN; imec/Samsung Si/SiGe stacks; no 3D DRAM use found (via search snippet).

key_insight: A tier carrying its own oxide periphery needs no FEOL. Passive interposers, glass and any logic BEOL then become DRAM hosts. I-11198 and the display ideas silently assume this enabler.
killer_doubt: Oxide-TFT Vt sigma of ~30-100 mV rivals a ~100 mV bitline signal, so n-only latches need offset cancellation. Mobility of ~10-30 cm2/Vs may make periphery 3-10x larger than in Si.
decisive_experiment: On an IGZO BEOL shuttle or university line, tape out a 1 kb 2T0C array with bootstrapped n-only decoders and auto-zeroed sense amps. Measure read time, margin, energy and Vt drift at 85 C (~$400k).
prior_art: No all-oxide DRAM periphery found (via search snippet). PragmatIC Flex-RV NMOS-only IGZO processor (Nature 2024); SEL CAAC-IGZO logic; display gate-on-array drivers.

key_insight: The silicon interposer is ~2,500 mm2 of already-paid silicon directly under the compute die. Memory tiers there could add ~100 GB at sub-pJ/bit with no TSVs.
killer_doubt: A passive interposer has no transistors for sense amps. Each 40 nm 1T1C tier needs a ~5 fF HAR capacitor. Flagship packages are shifting to CoWoS-L organic interposers.
decisive_experiment: Build a yield-and-cost model plus one coupon: a 2-tier oxide gain-cell array (not 1T1C) with IGZO periphery on an interposer-class 65 nm BEOL. Measure retention at 95 C under a hot die (~$350k).
prior_art: Duplicate of Phase B N-50 (gain-cell interposer). CEA-Leti IntAct active interposer; TSMC deep-trench capacitors in CoWoS interposers; no DRAM-tier interposer found (training knowledge).
